NSW Police PCT

NSW Police Physical Capacity Test

POLICE ENTRY TEST

At a glance

New South Wales Police uses six fitness activities for applicants. The requirements include a multi-stage fitness test (often called a beep test), alongside strength and agility activities.

FEATURED ACTIVITYMulti-stage fitness test20 m · level 7.1 required

What the test includes

  • 30 kg handgrip in each hand
  • 90-second prone bridge
  • 30 cm vertical jump
  • 25 push-ups
  • Illinois agility in 20 seconds or less
  • Multi-stage fitness test: level 7.1

Some programmes include more than the activities listed here.

Test protocol and standards

Six activities for general NSW Police recruitment. The professional mobility and cadet programmes use different criteria.

Official information checked 2026-11-24. Confirm current requirements with the test publisher.

EventMinimumAttempts
Grip strength30 kg each hand2
Prone bridge90 s1
Vertical jump30 cm2
Push-ups251
Illinois agility20 s or faster2
20 m shuttle runLevel 7.11

Scoring and scope

Each activity has its own minimum. For the 20 m shuttle, reach the line with a foot and pivot; the official protocol allows one warning for incorrect turns or line contact before stopping the participant on the second occurrence.

  • 20 m shuttle test instructions
  • Recruitment pathway information

How to prepare

Independent training guidance, not official test instructions. Scale sessions to your current capacity and recover between demanding efforts.

  • Mark a measured 20 m lane and practise controlled turns with the correct audio; use short blocks initially, not repeated maximal tests.
  • Train grip, strict push-ups and trunk endurance two or more non-consecutive days as tolerated; practise vertical jumps with adequate recovery.
  • Learn the official agility layout and practise acceleration and deceleration at increasing speed. Rehearse the six events as a battery only when familiar.

Putting it into a training week

Combine easy aerobic work with separate short agility and shuttle sessions. Grip, push-up and bridge work can be practised after easier sessions, provided form remains consistent.

Common mistakes

  • Using the 15 m UK police audio or an unmeasured lane.
  • Rounding the corners in a shuttle, counting invalid repetitions, or training only the beep test.

What to log

Track both handgrip results, bridge time, jump height, valid push-ups, agility time and level/shuttle.

Avoid repeated maximal tests and sudden load increases. Stop if pain, dizziness or unusual symptoms occur; use qualified supervision where appropriate.

Official test instructions

The organisation running the test is the best place to check the latest rules and requirements.
